title: Discovery of carbon monoxide emission from five debris disks around young A-type stars
question: Expand the sample of known CO-bearing debris disks around young intermediate-mass stars and explore the environmental conditions and origin (primordial vs. secondary) of their gas.

data.sensitivity: Continuum: 13.0-27.3 uJy/beam; 12CO: 1.6-5.0 mJy/beam/ch; 13CO: 0.8-1.4 mJy/beam/ch; C18O: 0.6-1.2 mJy/beam/ch

what.value: Geometric distance estimates based on Gaia EDR3 parallaxes

evidence.quote: Distance estimates are taken from (cite: bailerjones2021) using their geometric approach that is based only on the Gaia EDR3 parallaxes.
The $B_\mathrm{p}-R_\mathrm{p}$ colors were dereddened using data from the `Stilism` 3D database (cite: capitanio2017; lallement2018).

what.value: Table of stellar parameters of dwarf stars

evidence.quote: The spectral type was estimated based on the $B_\mathrm{p}-R_\mathrm{p}$ color index, using the updated online database of stellar parameters of dwarf stars (cite: pecaut2013).

what.value: Comparison sample of 46 young dust-rich debris disks with ALMA CO measurements

evidence.loc: Sample of young dust-rich debris disks observed by the ALMA
evidence.quote: In the literature, we identified 46 additional debris disks around stars with spectral types from A to K that are similarly young and dust-rich and for which ALMA millimeter CO line measurements are available (cite: kospal2013; dent2014; lieman-sifry2016; marino2016; moor2017; moor2019; difolco2020; kral2020; schneiderman2021; lovell2021; rebollido2022).

external_data.citation: (cite: kospal2013; dent2014; lieman-sifry2016; marino2016; moor2017; moor2019; difolco2020; kral2020; schneiderman2021; lovell2021; rebollido2022)

what.value: Empirical belt radius vs stellar luminosity relationship

evidence.loc: Radial location of planetesimal belts in CO bearing debris systems
evidence.quote: Using spatially resolved millimeter observations of debris disks, (cite: matra2018) derived an empirical relationship between the radius of the belts and the luminosity of the central star. Figure [7](#fig:rdiskls) shows the updated version of this relationship based on a larger sample (cite: matra2025).

what.value: Ages of Sco-Cen subgroups (US, UCL, LCC)

evidence.quote: The ages for the US, UCL, and LCC subgroups of the Sco-Cen association, 10$\pm$3, 15$\pm$3, and 16$\pm$2 Myr, are taken from (cite: gagne2018).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, concatenate, and continuum-subtract ALMA visibility data
recipe.method: Calibrate with standard ALMA pipeline, concatenate multi-epoch MSs with CONCAT, recalculate weights with STATWT, and subtract continuum in uv-space with UVCONTSUB using a 1st-order polynomial

recipe.goal: Image 1.33 mm dust continuum and fit visibility models to derive disk geometry and flux
recipe.method: Image line-free channels with TCLEAN (multiscale) and fit visibilities using UVMULTIFIT with point source, elliptical Gaussian, single Gaussian ring, or double narrow ring models
key_parameters: multiscale scales = [0, 5, 15, 25] pixels; Briggs robust = 0.5 (natural for HD 144277, HD 176497; 1 arcsec taper for non-detections)
W_disk = 0.7 R_disk fixed for HD 176497, HD 112532, HD 141960, HD 145101
assumptions: 10% absolute flux calibration uncertainty added in quadrature

recipe.method: Calculate optically thin dust mass from 1.33 mm flux density, distance, blackbody dust temperature, and dust opacity
assumptions: Optically thin thermal emission at 1.33 mm dominated by large blackbody grains with T_BB(K) = 278 (L_*/L_sun)^0.25 (R_disk/au)^-0.5 (or T_BB = 60 K for HD 131960/HD 144277, 110 K for HD 31305 A, 20 K for HD 31305 B)

recipe.goal: Image CO isotopolog cubes, create moment 0 maps, and extract integrated line fluxes
recipe.method: Image with TCLEAN, integrate channels with >3sigma emission in continuum disk region using custom IDL routines to build moment 0 maps, and extract line fluxes using elliptical curve-of-growth apertures
key_parameters: Channel width 0.4 km/s (12CO) and 1.6 km/s (13CO, C18O); 20 random off-source apertures for uncertainty estimation; 9% upward scaling for HD 155853 12CO flux due to <60m baseline cut
assumptions: For non-detections, gas is co-located with dust in Keplerian rotation to define integration velocity range

recipe.goal: Estimate CO optical depths and total CO gas masses
recipe.method: Derive 12CO optical depth from 12CO/13CO flux ratios and compute total 12CO mass from optically thin isotopolog (13CO for CO-rich, 12CO for CO-poor, C18O for HD 31305 B) assuming LTE at 20 K
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) at excitation temperature 20 K and ISM isotopic abundance ratios

recipe.goal: Analyze spatial distribution of CO gas via position-velocity (PV) diagrams and radial profiles
recipe.method: Construct 12CO PV diagrams along the disk major axis and compare with Keplerian rotation curves; fit ellipses to radial intensity peaks of moment 0 maps for HD 9985 and HD 155853; fit 2D Gaussian to HD 145101 moment 0 map
key_parameters: Radial cuts in 5 deg increments from 0 to 360 deg

recipe.goal: Evaluate CO detection rates, line luminosity distributions, collisional mass loss rates, and disk stirring mechanisms
recipe.method: Combine 11 targets with 46 literature disks; perform Fisher's exact tests on CO detection rates across stellar luminosity, fractional luminosity, and age; compute Kaplan-Meier CDFs with lifelines and logrank test; calculate steady-state collisional cascade mass loss rates; compute minimum self-stirring disk mass and planet stirring mass with MinSelfStirringDiscMass
key_parameters: Detection limit threshold L_12CO(2-1) > 9.5e16 W; planet eccentricity e = 0.3 for secular stirring
assumptions: Ideal steady-state collisional cascade; planetesimal belt inner/outer edges at R_disk +- 0.5 W_disk

recipe.goal: Derive fundamental stellar properties, association memberships, ages, and IR excess SEDs
recipe.method: Fit optical/near-IR photometry with ATLAS9/NEXTGEN models; evaluate group membership with BANYAN Sigma; fit MIST isochrones and lithium EW with eagles; fit IR excess SEDs with modified blackbody models using MPFIT
key_parameters: [Fe/H] = 0.0 +- 0.1; MBB break wavelength lambda_0 = 100 um; beta = 0.65 fixed when far-IR data absent
assumptions: Stars in young associations share the age of the association (except pre-MS star HD 145101)

answer_key.quantity: HD 145101 characteristic CO gas disk radius

evidence.quote: By fitting a two-dimensional elliptical Gaussian model to the $^{12}$CO moment 0 map of HD 145101, we found that its gas disk is marginally resolved and has FWHMs of 0.39$''$$\pm$0.11$''$$\times$0.30$''$$\pm$0.10$''$, implying a characteristic disk radius of 27$\pm$8 au.

answer_key.quantity: HD 152989 1.33 mm continuum flux density (single Gaussian ring)
HD 152989 continuum disk radius (single Gaussian ring)
HD 31305 B 1.33 mm continuum flux density

evidence.loc: The circumstellar disk of HD 31305 B
evidence.quote: We obtained a flux density of 2.37$\pm$0.24 mJy for the source, where the uncertainty is the quadratic sum of the measurement error (0.03 mJy) and the calibration error (assumed to be 10%).

evidence.loc: The circumstellar disk of HD 31305 B
evidence.quote: Based on the C$^{18}$O measurement, assuming that the line is optically thin and taking into account the above abundance ratio, we obtained a CO disk mass of 2.05$\pm$0.42$\times$10$^{-2}$ M$_\oplus$.

score_reason: Calibration,CASA versions, spectral setup, visibility modeling (UVMULTIFIT), and analytical equations for dust/gas masses and stirring are thoroughly documented with full parameter tables, though custom IDL scripts and exact moment-0 velocity windows/aperture sizes are not explicitly tabulated.
rediscovery_reason: Public Cycle 8 ALMA dataset (2021.1.01487.S) with clear numeric answer keys (continuum fluxes, ring radii, CO isotopolog line fluxes, optical depths, dust and CO masses) and standard visibility/image analysis steps.
